1.explanation:
• src/ol/renderer/webgl/TileLayer.js  
  This class owns the LRUCache of WebGLTileTexture objects. Its `getCacheKey(source, tileCoord)` key ties textures to a specific source object, but nothing in this file ever clears or resets that cache when `setSource()` is called or when the projection changes. As a result, old textures remain and are reused later.

• src/ol/renderer/webgl/Layer.js  
  The base WebGL renderer builds a `canvasCacheKey` in `prepareFrame()` using only the map ID and layer grouping. It never incorporates projection (or source) information, so the same WebGLHelper (and its underlying texture and render‐target caches) is reused across projection changes. The helper needs to be torn down or keyed by projection ID to force a fresh cache.

• src/ol/layer/WebGLTile.js  
  This high‐level layer listens for source‐change events (`handleSourceUpdate_`), but it does not trigger a cache reset on the renderer side. The layer should, on `setSource()`, call into the renderer (or clear the tile‐texture cache) so that stale textures aren’t reused after the source swap.
1.bug_scenario: When you switch the WebGL tile layer’s source at runtime (via `layer.setSource(...)`) or you switch the map view to a different projection, tiles already rendered into WebGL textures are never invalidated. In practice you’ll see the new source’s tiles (or the re-projected tiles) correctly load as you pan/zoom, but as soon as you pan back into areas you visited before the switch the old textures (from the old source or old projection) reappear. This is because neither the tile‐texture cache nor the rendering helper is ever flushed or recreated when the source or projection changes.
